- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias for 5–10 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean price; adjust downward by 1–4% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day trend for correction.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 7–14 days.
